blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Commercial Fitout Cost in Southbank in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Breaking down commercial fitout costs in Southbank for 2026: what to budget per square metre, hidden costs and how to save without compromising quality.
body: If you're planning a commercial fitout in Southbank in 2026, you're probably wondering what the bottom line looks like. Costs have shifted post-pandemic with supply chain adjustments and rising material prices. On average, a basic office fitout in Southbank can start around $800 per square metre, while a premium fitout with custom joinery and high-end finishes can push past $2,500 per square metre. These figures include partitioning, electrical, data cabling, flooring and painting — but exclude furniture and specialist AV equipment.

The exact cost depends heavily on the condition of your space. A shell or 'grey shell' fitout — where you start with bare concrete walls and exposed services — requires more work and budget than a refurbishment of an existing tenancy. In Southbank, many older buildings need additional fire services, accessible bathrooms and upgraded air conditioning to meet current standards. Factoring in a 10-15% contingency for unforeseen structural issues is always a wise move.

Location also matters. Southbank is a premium commercial precinct with high demand for office space near the CBD. Council approval times can vary, and if your fitout involves structural changes or heritage overlays, expect longer timelines and higher costs. Engaging a builder like 8Projects who knows Southbank's council requirements inside out can save you weeks of delays and thousands in compliance fees.

Labour costs in Melbourne remain competitive but skilled trades are in short supply. Carpenters, electricians and plasterers command premium rates, especially for fast-tracked projects. One way to keep costs down is to plan your fitout during quieter periods — avoid the end of financial year rush when everyone wants their office finished. A well-timed project can save 5-10% on labour.

Sustainability is becoming a major factor in commercial fitouts. Many Southbank businesses are opting for Green Star or NABERS-rated materials to attract eco-conscious tenants and reduce energy bills. While sustainable materials can carry a higher upfront cost, the long-term savings in electricity and water often offset the initial outlay. Plus, government incentives are available for energy-efficient upgrades.

Finally, always get multiple itemised quotes before committing. A fixed-price contract from a reputable builder like 8Projects ensures no surprises. Look for a quote that includes all preliminaries, waste disposal, permits and a defects liability period. The cheapest quote is rarely the best — invest in experience and local knowledge. Call 8Projects for a free, detailed breakdown tailored to your Southbank space.

blogPosts.title: Office Fitout Trends in Southbank for 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the latest office fitout trends hitting Southbank in 2026 — from biophilic design to hybrid-ready layouts, and how 8Projects can bring them to life.
body: Office design in Southbank is evolving fast. As businesses embrace hybrid working, the traditional cubicle farm is officially dead. In 2026, we're seeing a surge in flexible layouts that support both focused work and collaboration. Hot desking is out; activity-based working is in. That means more breakout zones, quiet pods, and bookable meeting rooms. 8Projects has been fitting out such spaces across Southbank, adapting older floorplates to meet modern needs.

Biophilic design — incorporating natural elements like plants, timber and natural light — continues to dominate. Studies show it boosts productivity and wellbeing. In Southbank, where many offices have floor-to-ceiling windows, we're maximising those views and adding living green walls. Reclaimed timber and stone finishes are popular choices that connect the indoors with the outdoors. These elements also help with acoustic control in open-plan areas.

Technology integration is another key trend. Touchless entry, smart lighting and occupancy sensors are becoming standard. Employees expect seamless connectivity, so robust data cabling and Wi-Fi 6 are non-negotiable. 8Projects works with specialist AV integrators to ensure your boardroom is video-conference ready, with proper soundproofing and lighting controls. Future-proofing your tech infrastructure is a smart investment for any Southbank business.

Wellness amenities are no longer a nice-to-have — they're expected. End-of-trip facilities like showers, bike storage and lockers are essential for attracting staff who cycle or run to work. Even small offices are carving out space for a wellness room or a quiet area. We're also seeing a rise in sit-stand desks and ergonomic furniture as part of the fitout package. These features can improve retention and reduce sick leave.

Colour palettes are shifting away from sterile whites towards warmer tones. Deep blues, greens and earthy neutrals create a calming yet professional atmosphere. Accent walls in brand colours or feature joinery add personality without overwhelming the space. Lighting is layered — ambient, task and accent — to reduce eye strain and create different moods throughout the day. 8Projects can source Australian-made joinery and lighting for a unique look.

If you're planning an office fitout in Southbank, now is the time to act. Tenancy availability is high, and landlords are offering fitout incentives to secure quality tenants. Partnering with an experienced local builder like 8Projects means you get a space that's not just beautiful but functional and compliant. Contact us for a consultation and let's design your 2026 office.

blogPosts.title: Retail Fitout Guide: Everything You Need to Know for Southbank Shops
blogPosts.excerpt: A complete guide to retail fitouts in Southbank: from permits and layout to fixtures and finishes. Learn how 8Projects creates spaces that drive foot traffic.
body: Opening a retail store in Southbank? A smart fitout can make the difference between a bustling shop and a quiet one. Southbank is a high-foot-traffic area with a mix of tourists, office workers and locals. Your fitout needs to grab attention instantly. 8Projects has delivered retail fitouts for cafes, boutiques and showrooms along Southbank Boulevard and surrounding streets. Here's what you need to know.

The first step is understanding council requirements. Southbank falls under the City of Melbourne, which has strict rules around signage, awnings and heritage protections if your building is listed. You'll need a building permit for most structural changes, and possibly a planning permit for changes to the facade. 8Projects handles all approvals, liaising directly with council to avoid delays. We recommend starting the permit process at least 8 weeks before you plan to open.

Layout is critical in retail. The customer journey should be intuitive — from the entrance to the display area, checkout and exit. We design for 'retail theatre': using lighting, colour and shelving to guide the eye. In small spaces, mirrors and glass can make the shop feel larger. Open sightlines deter theft and make the space feel welcoming. Our joinery team builds custom display units that maximise every square metre.

Lighting can make or break a retail space. Warm lighting suits clothing and homewares; cooler light works for electronics and groceries. Track lighting is versatile for changing displays, while accent lighting highlights key products. In Southbank, natural light is a bonus but can cause glare — we use adjustable blinds and UV film to protect stock and keep customers comfortable. Energy-efficient LED fittings also reduce your ongoing power bills.

Flooring and finishes need to withstand heavy foot traffic. Porcelain tiles, polished concrete and vinyl planks are popular choices for Southbank shops because they're durable and easy to clean. Timber adds warmth but requires more maintenance. We always recommend slip-resistant flooring near entrances, especially during Melbourne's rainy months. Wall finishes can be painted, tiled or clad in timber panels to create a signature look.

Finally, don't forget the back-of-house: storage, staff areas and a small kitchenette. Many retail fitouts allocate too little space to these, leading to clutter that affects the customer experience. 8Projects ensures your stockroom is organised with shelving and workbenches. We also install point-of-sale systems with concealed cabling for a clean look. Ready to start? Call 8Projects for a free site assessment and quote.

blogPosts.title: Bespoke Residential Construction in Southbank: What to Expect
blogPosts.excerpt: Building a custom home or renovating in Southbank? From heritage restrictions to townhouse designs, here's what 8Projects recommends for a successful project.
body: Southbank is known for its high-rise apartments and heritage-listed buildings, but there are also pockets of townhouses, terrace homes and infill sites where bespoke residential construction is thriving. 8Projects has completed a range of residential projects in and around Southbank, from heritage renovations to new townhouse developments. If you're considering building or renovating in this postcode, here's what you need to plan for.

Heritage overlays are common in parts of Southbank. If your property is heritage-listed or in a heritage precinct, you'll need approval from Heritage Victoria as well as the council. This can limit changes to the facade, windows and roofline. However, internal renovations are often more flexible. 8Projects has experience navigating these approvals and can recommend sympathetic materials that satisfy both the heritage guidelines and your modern lifestyle needs.

Townhouse construction is popular in Southbank's smaller streets. With land at a premium, maximising your site's potential is key. Many townhouses are built on narrow blocks (5-7 metres wide), requiring clever design to create a sense of space. Open-plan living, high ceilings and skylights are standard. 8Projects works with architects to design multi-level homes that feel light-filled and connected, even on tight sites.

Budget is always a concern. In Southbank, residential construction costs range from $2,500 to $4,000 per square metre depending on finishes and complexity. A knockdown-rebuild of a small terrace might cost $300k-$500k, while a high-end townhouse can exceed $1 million. We provide detailed cost plans upfront and track progress weekly to keep you informed. Fixed-price contracts are available for most projects.

Sustainability is a growing priority. Many Southbank residents want solar panels, rainwater tanks and energy-efficient glazing. The 7-star energy rating standard (coming into full effect) will soon be mandatory for new homes, so planning ahead saves future retrofit costs. 8Projects can incorporate passive design principles — orienting living areas north, using thermal mass and ensuring good cross-ventilation — to keep your home comfortable year-round.

Choosing the right builder is the most important decision. 8Projects brings commercial-grade project management to residential builds, meaning your timeline is realistic and your budget is respected. We involve you at every stage and never cut corners. From Southbank townhouses to heritage restorations, we deliver homes that last. Contact 8Projects for a no-obligation chat about your project.
